project.name: images-api
project.description: A Greenstand microservice that exposes a RESTful image resize API built with Express. It uses a layered MVC-like structure (protocol, service, and model layers) with a PostgreSQL database via Knex and Sharp for image processing.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: Express application factory that wires CORS, JSON body parsing, a content-type guard middleware, the API router, and the global error handler.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports a configured Express app instance via module.exports for reuse in tests and the server bootstrap.

nodes.name: app.spec.js
nodes.summary: Supertest/Chai test suite verifying the app rejects non-JSON POST requests with 415 and answers GET / with 200.

nodes.name: routes.js
nodes.summary: Express router mapping image-resize GET routes to the resize handlers, each wrapped by the async error-handling wrapper.

nodes.name: utils.js
nodes.summary: Express helper utilities providing an async handler wrapper and a centralized error handler that maps HttpError, Joi ValidationError, and Axios errors to HTTP responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses instanceof checks to branch error responses across HttpError, Joi ValidationError, and Axios error shapes.

nodes.name: handlerWrapper
nodes.summary: Higher-order wrapper that runs an async Express handler and forwards any rejected promise to next(), enabling throw-based error flow.

nodes.name: errorHandler
nodes.summary: Global Express error middleware translating HttpError, Joi ValidationError, and Axios errors into appropriate status codes and JSON bodies, defaulting to 500.

nodes.name: BaseRepository.js
nodes.summary: Generic Knex-backed data-access base class providing CRUD and filtered-query helpers for all repositories in the API model layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a recursive whereBuilder closure to translate nested and/or filter objects into chained Knex where clauses.

nodes.name: BaseRepository
nodes.summary: Base repository wrapping a Knex session to expose getById, getByFilter, countByFilter, update, and create operations against a configured table.

nodes.name: BaseRepository.spec.js
nodes.summary: Spec-named file that currently mirrors the BaseRepository CRUD implementation, defining the same Knex-backed repository class and importing HttpError.
nodes.languageNotes: Despite the .spec.js name, the file holds the production BaseRepository class rather than test assertions.

nodes.name: BaseRepository
nodes.summary: Repository class duplicated in the spec file, exposing getById, getByFilter, countByFilter, update, and create over a Knex session.

nodes.name: HttpError.js
nodes.summary: Defines a custom HttpError extending Error to carry an HTTP status code and a rollback flag, letting inner layers throw errors that outer layers convert to HTTP responses.

nodes.name: HttpError
nodes.summary: Error subclass storing an HTTP status code and a transaction rollback flag exposed via shouldRollback().

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build on node:16-alpine that installs dependencies via npm ci and runs the Express image-resize API with 'node .'.
nodes.languageNotes: Copies package files before source to leverage Docker layer caching for npm ci.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Empty Docker ignore file that would exclude paths from the Docker build context; currently no exclusions defined.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-build-deploy-dev.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline that runs on push to main; a test job lints and runs integration tests, then a release job publishes a semantic-release version, builds and pushes a Docker image to DockerHub, and updates the development kustomize overlay.
nodes.languageNotes: Two-stage pipeline using needs dependency; combines semantic-release, docker/build-push-action, and kustomize image edits for GitOps-style dev deployment.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-deploy-prod.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched GitHub Actions workflow that promotes a given image tag to the production kustomize overlay and commits the bump, gated to the Greenstand organization.
nodes.languageNotes: workflow_dispatch with a required git-tag input; edits deployment/overlays/production via kustomize.

nodes.languageNotes: workflow_dispatch with a required git-tag input; edits deployment/overlays/test via kustomize.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap
tour.description: The tour starts at the true entry point named in package.json. server.js loads environment configuration, sets the log level through setup.js, imports the Express app, and starts it listening on the configured port. This file is the thin outer shell of the microservice; it does no business logic itself and simply hands control to the app factory in Step 2.

tour.title: The Express App Factory
tour.description: app.js builds the Express application that server.js runs. It wires CORS, JSON body parsing, a content-type guard middleware, the image-resize router, and a single global error handler. This is the highest fan-out file in the codebase, so it gives a clear map of every layer the request passes through before a response returns.
tour.languageLesson: Express middleware runs in registration order. The final error-handling middleware uses four arguments (err, req, res, next), which is how Express recognises it as an error handler rather than a normal middleware.

tour.title: Routing and Request Dispatch
tour.description: routes.js is the controller layer of this MVC-style service. It maps the image-resize GET routes to their handlers and wraps each one in an async error-handling wrapper from the utility layer. Building on the app from Step 2, this file shows how an incoming URL is matched and dispatched to business code.

tour.title: Image-Resize Handlers
tour.description: resizeImageHandler.js sits between the router and the service layer. It reads and validates request parameters, then streams the resized image back to the client through the ResizeImageService. Note the handler only orchestrates HTTP concerns; the actual image work is delegated downward, keeping the protocol layer thin.

tour.title: The Service Layer: Sharp and Joi
tour.description: ResizeImageService.js holds the core business logic that gives this microservice its purpose. It fetches a remote source image over HTTP, validates the resize parameters (height, width, rotation, quality) with Joi, and applies the transforms with the Sharp image library. This is the deepest node in the dependency chain from the entry point and the payoff of the request flow started in Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: Sharp processes images as a stream pipeline, so large images never fully buffer in memory. Joi validates untrusted input against a schema before it reaches the transform stage, failing fast on bad parameters.

tour.title: Cross-Cutting Utilities and Error Handling
tour.description: The utility layer supports every other layer. utils.js provides the async handler wrapper (used by the router in Step 3) and the centralized error handler (registered by the app in Step 2), which maps HttpError, Joi validation errors, and Axios errors to proper HTTP responses. HttpError is the shared custom error type that lets inner layers throw and outer layers translate, while helper.js supplies pagination and query parsing. HttpError has the highest fan-in in the project.
tour.languageLesson: The async handler wrapper is a higher-order function: it wraps an async route handler and forwards any rejected promise to next(err), so a single error handler can catch failures from every route without repeated try/catch blocks.

tour.title: The Data Layer: Knex and Postgres
tour.description: Although the current image-resize flow is stateless, the template ships a full persistence layer. BaseRepository.js is a generic Knex-backed base class offering CRUD and filtered queries, Session.js manages the transaction lifecycle, and knex.js plus knexfile.js configure the shared Postgres connection per environment. This layer is the foundation for future repositories that store image or domain data.

tour.title: The API Contract
tour.description: The OpenAPI specification documents the public shape of the service independent of the code. It defines two GET endpoints: one that returns an image for a domain, and one that returns a resized image whose params encode height, width, rotation, and quality (for example h=100,w=100). Read this alongside the handlers from Step 4 to see how the documented contract maps onto the implementation.

tour.title: Testing Strategy
tour.description: The service is verified at two levels. app.spec.js is a focused unit test confirming the app rejects non-JSON POSTs with 415 and answers GET / with 200. image-resize-api.spec.js is an end-to-end integration suite that exercises the full Express app while mocking Axios, using the shared supertest helper as its HTTP client. Together they cover both the middleware guard from Step 2 and the resize flow from Steps 3 to 5.

tour.title: Project Manifest and Environment
tour.description: package.json is the project's control center: it declares server.js as the entry point, lists the lint, test, db-migrate, and seed scripts, and pins the Express, Knex, pg, and Sharp dependencies seen in earlier steps. The .env template documents the Postgres connection URLs and upstream API endpoints the service needs, and the README ties the whole layered protocol/service/model architecture together for new contributors.

tour.title: Containerization
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the service into a runnable image. It uses a single-stage build on node:16-alpine, installs dependencies with npm ci for reproducibility, and starts the app with 'node .', which resolves to the server.js entry point from Step 1. The .dockerignore controls what enters the build context.
tour.languageLesson: Layer ordering matters for Docker cache efficiency: copy package files and run npm ci before copying source, so a code change does not force a full dependency reinstall. npm ci installs exactly from the lockfile, giving deterministic builds.

tour.title: Kubernetes Deployment
tour.description: The container from Step 11 runs on Kubernetes, assembled with Kustomize. The base kustomization aggregates a namespace, a Deployment (one replica of the images-api container), a Service exposing the pods, and an Ambassador Mapping that routes external /images/ traffic into the service. This shows how the running process reaches real users in production.
tour.languageLesson: Kustomize separates a shared base from per-environment overlays: a base declares the common manifests, and development, test, and production overlays patch only what differs (mainly the image tag), avoiding duplicated YAML.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: GitHub Actions close the loop from commit to deployment. The pull-request workflow installs dependencies, runs ESLint, and executes the integration tests from Step 9 on every PR. The build-deploy-dev workflow runs on push to main, then publishes a semantic-release version, builds and pushes the Docker image from Step 11, and updates the development Kustomize overlay from Step 12. This is the capstone that automates the entire lifecycle.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers (pull_request, push) to decide when to run and 'jobs' with 'steps' to do the work. Gating deploy jobs to the source organization prevents forks from triggering releases.
